name: code-block
title: Code Block
description: Code in an AI answer, built for the fact that people paste it into real projects. `CodeBlock` takes `code`, optional `language` or `filename`, `streaming`, a pluggable `highlight(code, language)` renderer (bring Shiki or Prism, with no bundled grammar), `onApply` (sync or returning a promise), `showLineNumbers` and `collapseAfter`. While `streaming`, the header shows 'Writing' and Copy and Apply are disabled, so half a function can't be copied. Copy confirms 'Copied' or says 'Couldn't copy', both announced. Apply reports 'Applying', 'Applied' or 'Retry apply' from its promise. Long lines scroll horizontally by default, with a Wrap toggle. Blocks longer than `collapseAfter` lines (24) collapse behind 'Show all N lines'. The file also exports `splitCodeFences(markdown)`, which splits a possibly streaming markdown answer into text and code segments. An unclosed trailing fence becomes `{ complete: false }`, so it renders as a streaming CodeBlock instead of breaking layout. Use it in assistant messages, docs and diffs of generated code.
docs: Requires `cn` at `@/lib/utils`. Pass `streaming` while the fence is open. `splitCodeFences` tells you when that is. Highlighting is up to you: pass `highlight`, or leave it off for plain text.

meta.engineeringNotes: Built around the next action people take with generated code, which is copying it somewhere that matters. Streaming state is explicit: the group is `aria-busy`, the header reads 'Writing', and both Copy and Apply are disabled until the stream completes. Copy handles clipboard failure (permissions, insecure contexts) with a visible and announced 'Couldn't copy', because the silent alternative pastes stale clipboard contents. Apply is promise-aware, so the caller's real result drives 'Applying', 'Applied' or 'Retry apply'. `splitCodeFences` exists because markdown renderers handle an unclosed fence badly mid-stream. It detects fences with matching marker type and length (``` or ~~~, three or more), treats a trailing unclosed fence as an incomplete code segment, and leaves text segments for the caller's renderer. Highlighting is a render prop, so the registry item has zero dependencies and teams keep whichever highlighter their app already loads. Line numbers are a separate aria-hidden gutter computed from the line count, which works with any highlighter's output, and are hidden when wrapping, since wrapped lines would misalign them. A trailing newline is trimmed, so streams don't show a phantom empty line.
meta.motionNotes: Motion only for machine work. 'Writing' in the header and 'Applying' on the button take the shared `pd-shimmer`, because both are the machine's turn. The code itself never shimmers or animates in, since it is content. Button feedback ('Copied', 'Applied') is a text swap, not an animation, so it can be read immediately, and 'Copied' reverts after 2s. Hover colour runs at `--pd-duration-instant`. The collapse fade is static. Everything is static under prefers-reduced-motion.
